reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Quarterly Progress Report: October 2024 - December 2024

description.narrative:
Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) Grassroots, non-profit groups formed by community members to address local governance gaps and issues such as health, education, or development and overall. They often work directly with residents to implement programs and advocate for change.
Youth Convening & Serving Organizations Organizations focused on bringing young people together, providing services like leadership training, education, mentorship, and empowerment opportunities. They aim to support youth development and amplify their voices in society.
Government Officials (Duty Bearers) Elected or appointed public servants responsible for upholding laws, delivering services, and ensuring the rights of citizens are protected. They include civil servants, local administrators, and policy implementers.
Community Boundary Keepers (Village Elders, Church Leaders, Opinion Leaders) Influential local figures who uphold cultural norms, mediate conflicts, and guide community decisions. They play a key role in maintaining social cohesion and shaping public opinion.
Student Leaders Elected or recognized representatives of student bodies who advocate for the interests and welfare of their peers within educational institutions. They often liaise between students, administration, and external stakeholders.

The project aimed to empower youth as active participants in governance by creating inclusive and safe spaces for dialogue with government institutions and political actors. Through diverse platforms such as sports, art, community forums, and social media, the initiative engaged nearly 48,000 individuals, enabling broad civic participation. It strengthened the capacity of youth organizations to advocate for improved service delivery and hold leaders accountable, resulting in the resolution of key community challenges. By fostering collaboration between communities, institutions, and duty bearers, and promoting democratic values, the project enhanced youth awareness, leadership, and influence in shaping policies and driving social and economic development.
